outcome.Summary: Implemented the full expr language spec as Go package `expr/` (module example.com/expr): a byte-oriented lexer (expr/lexer.go) with all number/identifier/operator forms and `unexpected character` errors, a recursive-descent precedence parser (expr/parser.go) with the spec's precedence table — including right-associative `^` binding tighter than unary (`-2^2 = -4`, `2^-1 = 0.5`, `2^3^2 = 512`), C-style ternary with right-associative else branch — plus compile-time validation of built-in names/arities; a short-circuiting tree-walking evaluator (expr/expr.go) with math.Mod/ Pow semantics, division-by-zero, unknown-variable, sqrt-negative and non-finite-result *Error values at the specified positions; and the public API Error/Compile/Program.Eval/Program.Vars/Eval. Added ~120 table-driven test cases in expr/expr_test.go covering arithmetic/precedence, booleans, short-circuiting, ternary nesting, all built-ins, runtime and compile error messages/positions (exact-string checks), Vars sorting/dedup, and program reuse. Verified with `go vet ./... && go test ./...` (exit 0) and gofmt.
